what: The shipped Engine.dll created a real window in our own process through GAME::WinWindow::Initialize.

observed.handle_field_note: The object stored the handle at +0x08, not at +0x10 as the static reading of the parent-Window argument suggested; +0x10 stayed 0 because no parent was supplied.

discrepancy.fact: Calling Initialize with 800x600 produced a 130x100 client area.
discrepancy.meaning: The four integer arguments are not simply width/height as first assumed, or the Style value 1 constrains the size.
discrepancy.consequence: The exact argument semantics still need confirmation; this is recorded rather than smoothed over.

why_it_matters: Window creation is the first stage of the presentation path, and it now runs with original code: the export resolves, Initialize returns true, and the OS confirms a real window handle.
boundary: A window exists. No device, no swapchain and no presented frame exist yet, and the window was destroyed with the process.
next: Construct GraphicsEngine and call GraphicsEngine::CreateDevice(EWindow*, GraphicsEngineSettings&) so the engine loads direct3d11 and creates the device.
